findings.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching span-buf:s:* from SET to ZSET without a key migration or namespace change means live SET keys (TTL up to redis_ttl=3600s), during a rolling deploy or rollback, return WRONGTYPE on zadd, on the Lua zcard/zunionstore, and on flusher zscan. The non-transactional pipeline then raises for the whole batch, so consumer/flusher crash-loop and replay.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — zpopmin silently drops the earliest-ending spans once a segment passes 1000, with no metric or log (segment_span_count_exceeded was removed). It can evict the segment/root span itself (children that outlive the root, or SDK-controlled end timestamps), so the flush emits a rootless, truncated segment while hrs is still "1".

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — enable_advanced is computed on every request, even without optimized_pagination, and dereferences organization_context.member, which is None for permitted non-member callers (active staff that are not is_superuser, API-key auth). The existing audit-log endpoint now fails with AttributeError/500 for them.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on AuditLogEntry.datetime (a datetime), which raises TypeError inside build_cursor for any non-empty page, so the gated optimized path always 500s.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw client cursor number, which build_queryset compares to a timestamptz column ("datetime <= 1700000000000"), so any cursor with a value fails with a DB type error instead of paginating.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — The advanced branch slices the queryset with a client-supplied negative offset; Django raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported"), so the headline feature produces unhandled 500s and the comment claiming the ORM "handles negative slicing" is false.

tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:126 — Every test span uses the identical end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 and no test exceeds 1000 spans, so the eviction ordering and cap tests pass without being exercised (silent-pass), including root-span eviction and the cap.

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — ZUNIONSTORE uses the default AGGREGATE SUM, so a redelivered/replayed span (Kafka at-least-once, e.g. after the crash loop above) that is present in both set_key and parent_key gets its score doubled, which corrupts evict-by-end-timestamp ordering (that span becomes effectively unevictable).

src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — Cutting the redirect walk from 10000 to 1000 means chains deeper than 1000 (bottom-up out-of-order ingestion) stop at an intermediate set and are silently split into separate segments; the only signal is the max_redirect_depth gauge.

src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:150 — max_segment_spans is still accepted and stored but never used; the effective cap is hardcoded to 1000 in Lua, so an operator tuning this knob gets no effect and no error.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:71 — The "authorized administrators" gate checks the raw is_superuser DB flag (not is_active_superuser) or has_global_access, which is true for every member of an open-membership org, so it is not an admin check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Switching span-buf:s:* from SET to ZSET without a key migration or namespace change means live SET keys (TTL up to redis_ttl=3600s), during a rolling deploy or rollback, return WRONGTYPE on zadd, on the Lua zcard/zunionstore, and on flusher zscan. The non-transactional pipeline then raises for the whole batch, so consumer/flusher crash-loop and replay.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Redis data structure at the same key namespace `span-buf:s:{...}:...` from SET to ZSET: `buffer.py` switches `p.sadd(set_key, ...)` to `p.zadd(set_key, {payload: end_timestamp_precise})`, `_load_segment_data` switches `sscan` to `zscan`, and the Lua script switches `scard/sunionstore` to `zcard/zunionstore`. There is no namespace change or migration logic in the diff to handle existing live SET keys (which can exist due to TTL). During a rolling deploy/rollback, operations like `ZADD`, `ZSCAN`, `ZCARD`, `ZUNIONSTORE` against an existing SET key will raise Redis WRONGTYPE, and since the pipeline is non-transactional it can fail the batch, leading to consumer/flusher errors as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — zpopmin silently drops the earliest-ending spans once a segment passes 1000, with no metric or log (segment_span_count_exceeded was removed). It can evict the segment/root span itself (children that outlive the root, or SDK-controlled end timestamps), so the flush emits a rootless, truncated segment while hrs is still "1".

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a hard cap in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` that, when `span_count > 1000`, executes `redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)`. This unconditionally evicts the lowest-score members of the sorted set (with scores coming from `end_timestamp_precise` via `zadd` in `spans/buffer.py`), i.e., the earliest-ending spans. There is no protection to keep a segment/root span from being evicted, and the script’s `has_root_span` logic is based on the separate `span-buf:hrs` key (`get` == "1" or `is_root_span`), so it can still indicate a root exists even if the root payload was popped. Additionally, the previous Python-side guard/metrics for too many spans (`segment_span_count_exceeded`) was removed in `_load_segment_data`, so this introduces silent span loss/truncation behavior without metrics/logging in this path.

tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:126 — Every test span uses the identical end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 and no test exceeds 1000 spans, so the eviction ordering and cap tests pass without being exercised (silent-pass), including root-span eviction and the cap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new eviction/capping logic in `add-buffer.lua` using a sorted set score (`end_timestamp_precise`) and caps the set at 1000 via `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000`. In `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` (and other updated tests), the added `end_timestamp_precise` values are all the same constant `1700000000.0`, and the shown test cases only create a handful of spans—so neither the ordering-dependent behavior (evicting the lowest-score spans) nor the `> 1000` cap/eviction path is exercised. This is a concrete test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:53 — ZUNIONSTORE uses the default AGGREGATE SUM, so a redelivered/replayed span (Kafka at-least-once, e.g. after the crash loop above) that is present in both set_key and parent_key gets its score doubled, which corrupts evict-by-end-timestamp ordering (that span becomes effectively unevictable).

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the diff replaces `SUNIONSTORE` with `ZUNIONSTORE` (e.g. `span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` and similarly for `parent_key`) but does not specify `AGGREGATE`. Redis defaults `ZUNIONSTORE` aggregation to `SUM`, so if the same member (here, `span.payload` as the sorted-set member) exists in both inputs, its resulting score will be summed. Given `buffer.py` now stores spans via `zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise})`, summing would inflate `end_timestamp_precise` and distort the time-based ordering used later for eviction (`zpopmin`), which is a correctness bug exposed by this change.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` the redirect-walk loop limit is reduced from `0, 10000` to `0, 1000`. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the `datetime` key used by the audit-logs endpoint (TypeError: must be real number, not datetime), so every non-empty `optimized_pagination=true` response returns 500 and the path can never emit a valid Link cursor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:843 — value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value instead of converting it to a datetime, so epoch-ms cursors clients already hold from DateTimePaginator Link headers on the same endpoint become a `datetime <= <int>` SQL comparison, and the two modes' cursors are incompatible with each other.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — The advertised "negative offset support" slices the Django queryset with a negative start, which raises ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported"); that isn't caught as BadPaginationError, so client cursors like `x:-5:0` produce a 500 instead of a 400.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — zunionstore uses the default AGGREGATE SUM, so a payload present in both sets (for example a redelivered span) ends up with the sum of its end timestamps as its score, which corrupts the zpopmin eviction order; it should use AGGREGATE MAX or MIN.

adjudication.rationale:
In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the diff replaces `sunionstore` with `zunionstore`:
```lua
span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)
...
span_count = redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, parent_key)
```
No `AGGREGATE` option is provided. Redis `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so if the same member (here the member is `span.payload`) exists in both input zsets, its resulting score will be the sum of the two scores. Since scores are set to `end_timestamp_precise` (via `zadd` in `spans/buffer.py`) and eviction later uses `zpopmin` to drop the oldest by score, summed scores can incorrectly make an older/duplicate span appear newer, corrupting eviction order and retention behavior. This is a correctness issue introduced by the change to zsets/unioning without an explicit aggregation strategy.

From the diff we can verify the config-based cap is no longer applied in Python and the effective cap is now hard-coded in Lua, which makes `max_segment_spans` (if still configured elsewhere) ineffective and could be surprising/undesired behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — Spans evicted by zpopmin keep their span-buf:sr redirect entries because done_flush_segments only hdels span_ids that were flushed, so the redirect entries leak and later children of evicted spans are routed into the stale segment key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:434 — ZSCAN on leftover SET segment keys raises WRONGTYPE for the whole flush pipeline, so done_flush_segments never runs. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — ZUNIONSTORE uses the default SUM aggregate, so a span re-delivered on Kafka replay after a crash ends up with a summed (doubled) score, which skews eviction order.
